proof_summary: Pell pairs \((p_n,q_n)\) satisfying \(p_n^2+2p_nq_n-q_n^2=1\) give upper approximations \(p_n/q_n\) to \(\sqrt2-1\) with error below \(1/q_n^2\), so for \(1\le k\le q_n\) the relevant floor is exactly \(\lfloor(kp_n-1)/q_n\rfloor\). Grouping these rationalized terms by exponent and using the oddness of \(p_n\) yields the recurrence \(a(q_{n+1})=a(q_n)+2\), hence \(a(q_n)=2(n+1)\) and the values are unbounded.
